question: persister
prompt:
Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

Work in two steps. First, in the candidates field, brainstorm 20 candidate ideas, one line each, covering as wide a range as you can. Then select the 5 candidates that best combine being non-obvious with being feasible and informative, and develop those as your ideas.

ideas.title: Lineage barcoding with split-sample single-cell RNA-seq
ideas.description: Barcode a clonal population, split it before drug, profile one arm by scRNA-seq and treat the other, then identify which barcodes survive. This lets you read out the pre-treatment transcriptional state of cells destined to become persisters and test whether it is heritable.

ideas.title: Luria-Delbrück fluctuation analysis of persister frequency
ideas.description: Expand many small independent clones, treat each, and compare the variance in persister counts to that expected under pre-existing versus drug-induced tolerance. Fitting a state-switching model to the data yields switching rates and distinguishes stochastic state fluctuations from stable epigenetic or genetic inheritance.

ideas.title: Live-cell reporter imaging with retrospective pedigree tracing
ideas.description: Image cells for days before and after drug with reporters for signaling (ERK, p53), cell cycle (FUCCI) and stress, then trace surviving cells back through their lineage. This shows whether dynamics, cycle history or sister-cell correlations predict survival, which fixed snapshots cannot show.

ideas.title: Sort-then-challenge on pre-treatment physiological state
ideas.description: Use FACS to sort untreated cells by mitochondrial potential, ROS, drug efflux activity, or fluorescent drug uptake, then treat each sorted fraction and measure persister yield. This tests causality of candidate states and how long they last by delaying the drug challenge after sorting.

ideas.title: Persister-fraction-focused CRISPR and epigenetic perturbation screens
ideas.description: Run pooled CRISPRi/a or epigenetic-inhibitor screens that read out the fraction of surviving cells at a fixed high dose, not bulk sensitivity. Hits that change only the persister fraction point to regulators of cell-state plasticity, and comparing them with scATAC/multiome data in persisters links them to chromatin mechanisms.

candidates: Lineage barcoding (e.g., ClonMapper) to test whether persisters arise from pre-existing heritable states or stochastically
Fluctuation test (Luria-Delbrück) on drug-tolerant persisters to distinguish pre-existing vs induced tolerance
Time-lapse live-cell imaging with fluorescent reporters tracing persisters backward to pre-treatment state
Single-cell RNA-seq before and at multiple times after drug exposure
Paired barcode-based single-cell RNA-seq of sister cells split before treatment
Single-cell ATAC-seq / multiome for chromatin accessibility of persisters
Mitochondrial content and membrane potential sorting before treatment followed by drug challenge
Single-cell proteomics/CyTOF of signaling network states (MAPK, PI3K) pre- and post-drug
Pooled CRISPR screens for genes that modulate persister fraction (not bulk IC50)
Cell-cycle state tracking with FUCCI and quiescence/slow-cycling analysis
Single-cell metabolomics or NAD(P)H/FLIM imaging of metabolic state
Measure drug uptake/efflux and intracellular drug concentration per cell using fluorescent drug analogs
Epigenetic inhibitor combination screens (HDAC, KDM5, EZH2) to alter persister fraction
Whole-genome sequencing of persisters to rule out or find rare genetic/extrachromosomal DNA changes
Oxidative stress and lipid peroxidation (ferroptosis) reporters in persisters
Mathematical modeling of state-switching rates fit to fluctuation and lineage data
Spatial transcriptomics of 3D spheroids/xenografts to test microenvironmental positioning
Single-cell tracking of transcription factor dynamics (e.g., p53, ERK pulses) under drug
Heritability of persistence across divisions via sister-cell pedigree analysis
Stress-response/translation profiling (ribosome profiling, integrated stress response) in persisters
Mitotic timing and DNA damage/ replication stress marker analysis in drug-treated cells
